exact_factorization_on_Eq.derivation: Substitute y^2=x(x+1)(x+q^2) into the Face-3 formula and factor the numerator exactly.
exact_factorization_on_Eq.consequence: Away from the poles x=+/-q, F3(Q) is a rational square iff A_q(x)B_q(x) is a rational square.

genus5_cover.receiver_equivalence: For non-pole Q in E_q(Q), F3(Q) square iff Q lies in the projection of C_q(Q).

branch_check.A_B_common_root_excluded_by: B_q-(1+q^2)A_q=4*q^2*x; for q!=0 a common root would force x=0, but A_q(0)=q^2!=0

finite_squareclass_descent.setup: Write q=a/b in lowest positive terms and x=X/Z with gcd(X,Z)=1.
finite_squareclass_descent.gcd_support_proof: For p not dividing 2ab, a common divisor would force p|XZ. If p|X then A_h=a^2 Z^2 mod p is nonzero; if p|Z then A_h=b^2 X^2 mod p is nonzero, using gcd(X,Z)=1.
finite_squareclass_descent.square_consequence: If A_h*B_h is a square, then there is a positive squarefree d supported on primes dividing 2ab with A_h=d*u^2 and B_h=d*v^2.
finite_squareclass_descent.purpose: Turn the global square problem into a finite 2-cover/squareclass collection before elliptic-Chabauty or Mordell-Weil-sieve work.
